fixture.name: Synthetic 12 unique case_id series with two points each

math_bound: For each case ID i, each PromQL matcher m tests label value li(k) or '' when key k is absent. = and != use string comparisons; =~ and !~ use regex fullmatch. Native sum by(case_id)(last_over_time(metric{m}[5m])) must emit exactly (case_id_i,T,i+101) for every matching series. Because case_id is unique, grouping has no numeric rounding ambiguity. Any different key or value falsifies the oracle.
method: One isolated ubuntu-24.04 Actions job, actual native prometheusQueryRange, source and executable SHA checks. 21 distinct matcher cases applied before and after verified physical part merge. No C++ modifications; no direct SQL substitute; independent Python matcher oracle. Exactly one timestamp per resulting case_id.
limitations: No NaN/Inf, staleness, reset, duplicate timestamp, late write, ACL or cross-tenant authorization test.
Only one fixed small fixture and the lab O1 binary. No independent VictoriaMetrics/Prometheus server oracle.
The Python regex oracle uses fullmatch on simple regex patterns also supported by PromQL. Complex RE2 features are not covered.
No load, wall/CPU or production performance claims.
stop_condition: Do not promote source fast paths on this gate alone. Stop if any oracle case differs or the physical part-count guard fails.

next_action.step: Run separate small native PromQL differential test for counter reset, out-of-order/duplicate samples, stale-NaN and TTL boundaries using independent reference/VM; compare across part merges and restarts.
next_action.stop_condition: Any parity mismatch, ingestion rejection or unsupported semantics must be classified separately and not hidden as successful benchmark.
